name: Hiking Checklist
description: A day hike checklist covering the ten essentials, clothing layers, food and water, navigation and trail safety.

items.text: Trail map and a guidebook or printout
Compass and the knowledge to use it
GPS device or a phone with offline maps
items.note: Download the trail map in case you lose signal.

items.text: Fully charged phone and a power bank
Note of trail name, distance, and elevation gain
Sunscreen and lip balm with SPF
Sunglasses with UV protection
Brimmed hat or cap
Insect repellent
Lightweight rain jacket or shell
Broken-in hiking boots or trail shoes
Moisture-wicking base layer
Insulating layer such as a fleece
Extra socks
Warm hat and gloves for higher elevations
Quick-dry hiking pants or shorts
Water bottles or a hydration reservoir
Water filter or tablets if refilling on the trail
Trail snacks: nuts, bars, dried fruit
A packed lunch for longer hikes
Electrolyte mix for hot days
Compact first-aid kit with blister care
Headlamp or flashlight with extra batteries
Whistle for signaling
Emergency shelter such as a space blanket
Fire starter and waterproof matches
Personal medications
Multi-tool or knife
Repair tape and a few zip ties
Trekking poles for steep terrain
Small trash bag to pack out litter
Hand sanitizer and tissues
ID and emergency contact card
Check the weather and trail conditions
Tell someone your route and return time
items.note: Agree on when to raise the alarm if you are overdue.

items.text: Confirm parking, permits, and trail access
Start early to finish before dark
Know your turnaround time and stick to it

faq.q: What are the ten essentials for hiking?
faq.a: The ten essentials are navigation, sun protection, insulation, illumination, first-aid supplies, fire, a repair kit and tools, nutrition, hydration, and emergency shelter. Carrying all ten means you can handle an unexpected delay or emergency on the trail.

faq.q: What should I pack for a day hike?
faq.a: Pack a daypack with water, snacks, a map or GPS, sun protection, extra layers, a first-aid kit, a headlamp, and a fully charged phone. Wear broken-in footwear and dress in layers you can add or remove as conditions change.

faq.q: How much water should I bring hiking?
faq.a: Plan for about half a liter of water per hour of moderate hiking, and more in heat or at altitude. Carry enough for the full route plus a reserve, or bring a filter if reliable water sources are available along the way.

faq.q: Can I print this hiking checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as you load your daypack before the trail.

faq.q: How do I stay safe on a day hike?
faq.a: Check the weather and trail conditions before you go, tell someone your route and expected return time, and stay on marked trails. Carry the ten essentials, turn back if conditions worsen, and know your limits.
